metrics.name: Net awarded marks
metrics.inputs: signed contributions under the current approved key.
metrics.formula: S = sum(score_q), including explicitly identified awards.
metrics.evidence: a finalized grading revision; otherwise show grading pending.
metrics.action: inspect the largest lost-mark contributors and any adjustment notice.
metrics.limitation: raw marks compare directly only within the same scoring context; they do not indicate national rank or percentile.

metrics.name: Fully correct response count
metrics.inputs: final committed response and full-correct evaluation outcome.
metrics.formula: C = count(full_correct).
metrics.evidence: all relevant items graded; preserve a pending count if any remain unresolved.
metrics.action: revisit correct answers whose reasoning felt uncertain.
metrics.limitation: an observed correct answer can result from guessing or prior exposure and does not establish concept mastery.

metrics.name: Incorrect and partial outcomes
metrics.inputs: distinct evaluation outcomes.
metrics.formula: W = count(incorrect), P = count(partial_credit); display both separately within this analysis.
metrics.evidence: approved adapter classification.
metrics.action: open the wrong list first, then examine why partial answers failed full-credit criteria.
metrics.limitation: a partially correct multiselect response is not equivalent to a wrong single-choice answer; do not flatten their explanations.

metrics.name: Attempted-answer accuracy
metrics.inputs: C and A = C + P + W.
metrics.evidence: A > 0; show the exact fraction for any A, but suppress strength labels below 10 attempts.
metrics.action: inspect inaccurate attempted topics before increasing attempts blindly.
metrics.limitation: excluding unanswered items can make selective students look stronger; pair this value with completion and partial-credit counts.

metrics.name: Response completion rate
metrics.inputs: attempted A and eligible delivered E.
metrics.formula: 100 * A / E, with unanswered count E - A.
metrics.evidence: E > 0 and submission finalized.
metrics.action: distinguish unvisited questions from viewed but unanswered questions before planning coverage.
metrics.limitation: completion rewards submitting a response, not correct reasoning; high completion can coexist with negative marks and poor accuracy.

metrics.name: Ordinary positive marks earned
metrics.inputs: ordinary item contributions s_q.
metrics.formula: G = sum(max(s_q, 0)), excluding separate award-only adjustments B.
metrics.evidence: finalized ordinary grading.
metrics.action: identify which subjects and question types generate the positive marks.
metrics.limitation: G ignores penalties and is not the final result; partial-credit contributions remain positive marks rather than full-correct counts.

metrics.name: Penalty marks lost
metrics.inputs: negative ordinary contributions.
metrics.formula: L = sum(max(-s_q, 0)).
metrics.evidence: finalized grading; zero is valid when the preset has no negative marking.
metrics.action: review the exact penalized responses and their stated confidence where available.
metrics.limitation: a penalty does not prove an irresponsible guess; a student may have made a sincere reasoning error.

metrics.name: Penalty-to-positive-marks ratio
metrics.inputs: L and G.
metrics.evidence: G > 0; otherwise show L with ratio unavailable.
metrics.action: compare the ratio across comparable first attempts and inspect preventable error categories.
metrics.limitation: values may exceed 100 percent; do not clamp them. This is not penalty divided by final net marks, which becomes unstable near zero.

metrics.name: Percentage of configured maximum marks
metrics.inputs: total S and current effective maximum M from the scoring policy.
metrics.evidence: M > 0 and all special awards resolved.
metrics.action: read alongside raw marks to understand the scale of this paper.
metrics.limitation: allow negative percentages where rules permit negative scores; this percentage is not a cohort percentile or an official normalized score.

metrics.name: Subject marks contribution
metrics.inputs: item-to-subject assignment and signed contributions.
metrics.formula: S_subject = sum(s_q within subject); show G_subject, L_subject and awards separately.
metrics.evidence: every item has one approved primary scoring subject.
metrics.action: choose a subject for detailed review based on its actual mark losses and coverage.
metrics.limitation: subjects with different item counts or time demands cannot be judged solely by raw totals.

metrics.name: Chapter mark contribution
metrics.inputs: approved chapter tags, item score and tag weights.
metrics.formula: sum(w_qg * s_q), where weights across a question's assigned chapters sum to one.
metrics.evidence: reviewed chapter mapping; show recommendations only for groups with at least 10 attempts.
metrics.action: locate chapters contributing losses.
metrics.limitation: fractional attribution is an accounting convention, not a measurement of each chapter's causal role.

metrics.name: Concept attempted accuracy
metrics.inputs: fully correct and attempted items matching one approved concept.
metrics.formula: 100 * C_concept / A_concept.
metrics.evidence: denominator positive; advice requires at least 10 distinct items across two sessions.
metrics.action: inspect repeated reasoning errors within the concept.
metrics.limitation: overlapping tags make separate concept cards nonadditive, and unequal item difficulty can distort comparisons.

metrics.name: Response-type performance
metrics.inputs: response type, signed marks and configured maxima.
metrics.formula: sum(s_q) / sum(max_q), separately for single-choice, numerical and supported multiselect categories.
metrics.evidence: positive maximum; recommend changes only above 10 items per type.
metrics.action: compare handling of input and selection tasks.
metrics.limitation: response-type differences may reflect topic and marking differences rather than input skill.

metrics.name: Editorial difficulty outcome matrix
metrics.inputs: human-approved difficulty labels and final outcomes.
metrics.formula: C/A and net marks within each editorial band, with unanswered counts.
metrics.evidence: at least 10 attempted items per band for interpretation; unknown labels remain a separate row.
metrics.action: identify easier-band errors worth checking first.
metrics.limitation: editorial difficulty is a judgment and must not masquerade as nationally calibrated difficulty.

metrics.name: First-exposure versus repeat performance
metrics.inputs: canonical item exposure history and solution access before the attempt.
metrics.formula: C/A separately for unseen, previously seen and solution-exposed items.
metrics.evidence: known exposure history and at least 10 attempts per compared group.
metrics.action: favor fresh questions when checking transfer.
metrics.limitation: remembered answers and self-selected repeats inflate performance; cross-group gaps do not estimate the effect of studying.

metrics.name: Timer time consumed
metrics.inputs: server start, effective deadline, authorized adjustments and submission receipt.
metrics.formula: min(submitted_at, deadline_at) - started_at, adjusted by documented timer rules.
metrics.evidence: complete server clock ledger.
metrics.action: examine whether substantial available time remained at submission.
metrics.limitation: elapsed time includes offline or hidden-page periods in an unpaused timed exam; it does not measure active thinking.

metrics.name: Observed visible question time
metrics.inputs: question-enter, question-leave, visibility and capped heartbeat intervals.
metrics.formula: union duration of valid visible intervals attributed to each question, summed without overlap.
metrics.evidence: valid timestamp order and coverage flags.
metrics.action: compare where observable attention was allocated.
metrics.limitation: visibility does not establish mental focus, and a static visible page may still be actively read.

metrics.name: Unobserved timer fraction
metrics.inputs: timer duration D, visible attributed T and recorded hidden duration H.
metrics.formula: 100 * max(D - T - H, 0) / D after interval reconciliation.
metrics.evidence: D > 0; distinguish known hidden time from missing events.
metrics.action: inspect connection or telemetry gaps before trusting timing advice.
metrics.limitation: unobserved time must not be called laziness, cheating or distraction.

metrics.name: Time on slow incorrect responses
metrics.inputs: wrong items, observed time and approved per-item correct-response median.
metrics.formula: sum(T_q where incorrect and T_q > 2 * benchmark_q).
metrics.evidence: five usable wrong items and at least 30 correct cohort times per benchmark.
metrics.action: review stopping and revisiting tactics.
metrics.limitation: this descriptive threshold is configurable; slow errors may reflect legitimate effort, not wasted thought.

metrics.name: Question budget overrun
metrics.inputs: a student-approved pretest time budget b_q and observed T_q.
metrics.formula: sum(max(T_q - b_q, 0)); list individual overruns.
metrics.evidence: budget existed before the attempt and valid timing; otherwise unavailable.
metrics.action: adjust the next practice budget after reviewing difficulty.
metrics.limitation: the overrun is measured against a plan, not an optimal schedule or guaranteed lost marks.

metrics.name: Subject time allocation
metrics.inputs: valid question-visible time and primary subject.
metrics.formula: 100 * T_subject / sum(T_subject), alongside absolute minutes.
metrics.evidence: positive observed time and at least 90 percent usable item timing.
metrics.action: compare allocation with the student's pretest plan and mark contribution.
metrics.limitation: equal subject time is not inherently desirable; different papers and personal strengths require different allocations.

metrics.name: First-visit duration
metrics.inputs: each eligible item's first valid visible visit.
metrics.formula: median(first_visit_seconds), with a distribution by outcome.
metrics.evidence: at least five usable first visits per reported group.
metrics.action: identify where an initial scan became an extended attempt.
metrics.limitation: first-visit time may include reading shared passages or diagrams; it is not pure solution time.

metrics.name: Revisit time share
metrics.inputs: visible visits ordered per item.
metrics.formula: 100 * sum(duration of visits after the first) / total attributed time.
metrics.evidence: positive total and at least five visited items.
metrics.action: inspect whether revisits resolved uncertainty or repeated an unproductive approach.
metrics.limitation: a high revisit share can be a sensible checking strategy; it is not automatically inefficient.

metrics.name: Positive score difference after revisions
metrics.inputs: first committed response, final response and current scoring policy.
metrics.formula: sum(max(score(final_q) - score(first_commit_q), 0)).
metrics.evidence: complete commitments for revised items; show exact differences after one revision.
metrics.action: review the reasoning behind beneficial changes.
metrics.limitation: this compares recorded endpoints and cannot prove that changing answers caused improvement or predict future gains.

metrics.name: Negative score difference after revisions
metrics.inputs: the same committed endpoints.
metrics.formula: sum(max(score(first_commit_q) - score(final_q), 0)).
metrics.evidence: complete revision history; annotate clears and timeout acceptance rules.
metrics.action: study harmful changes and the evidence used to justify them.
metrics.limitation: final correctness is hindsight; do not prescribe never changing answers from one outcome or count uncommitted drafts as lost marks.

metrics.name: Late-window attempted accuracy
metrics.inputs: time of first accepted response commitment and final outcome.
metrics.formula: C/A for items first committed in the final 20 percent of authorized duration versus earlier items.
metrics.evidence: at least 10 items in each group and valid timestamps.
metrics.action: review late errors and pace planning.
metrics.limitation: late items may be harder or from another subject; the gap does not diagnose fatigue.

metrics.name: Recovery of unanswered review items
metrics.inputs: items first marked for review while unanswered and their final outcomes.
metrics.formula: recovered full-correct items / initially unanswered review items.
metrics.evidence: at least five such items and ordered review events.
metrics.action: examine which revisit choices converted omissions into correct responses.
metrics.limitation: a review flag is an interface state, and successful recovery does not reveal the optimal review order.

metrics.name: Unvisited eligible-item rate
metrics.inputs: delivered ordinary items and successful question-render events.
metrics.formula: 100 * count(no render recorded) / E.
metrics.evidence: E > 0, reconciled navigation events and at least 95 percent timer duration accounted for by known visible or hidden intervals.
metrics.action: practice an initial scan if entire sections were missed.
metrics.limitation: missing render events can mimic unvisited questions; show unavailable when navigation evidence is incomplete.

metrics.name: Time spent on viewed omissions
metrics.inputs: final unanswered items with recorded visits and visible duration.
metrics.formula: sum(T_q for viewed and unanswered items), with count and question list.
metrics.evidence: valid item timings and at least 90 percent relevant coverage.
metrics.action: review whether a timely skip or an alternate method would help.
metrics.limitation: unanswered effort may improve understanding; do not automatically classify these minutes as waste.

metrics.name: Median time on fully correct items
metrics.inputs: visible attributed durations for fully correct responses.
metrics.formula: median(T_q), split by subject or response type.
metrics.evidence: at least five correct timed items per personal group.
metrics.action: identify unusually long correct solutions to compare with an approved shorter method.
metrics.limitation: faster is not always better, and comparing unlike item mixtures can give a misleading speed conclusion.

metrics.name: Overall platform cohort percentile
metrics.inputs: the learner's net score s and eligible cohort scores.
metrics.formula: 100 * count(score <= s) / N.
metrics.evidence: N >= 100; otherwise suppress the percentile.
metrics.action: compare standing on this specific mock while reviewing subject gaps.
metrics.limitation: this self-selected platform cohort is not the official exam population; an apparent rise can reflect cohort changes.

metrics.name: Subject platform cohort percentile
metrics.inputs: approved subject net scores for the same cohort.
metrics.formula: 100 * count(subject_score <= learner_subject_score) / N.
metrics.evidence: N >= 100 and common subject scoring.
metrics.action: identify subjects with weaker relative standing on this paper.
metrics.limitation: never average subject percentiles to produce total percentile; ties and differing distributions prevent that shortcut.

metrics.name: Item full-correct cohort proportion
metrics.inputs: one binary-eligible item's full-correct outcomes and all eligible delivered attempts.
metrics.formula: p_q = C_q / N_q, including unanswered responses in N_q.
metrics.action: check wrong answers on widely solved questions first.
metrics.limitation: this is a cohort response statistic, not the student's question-wise ability percentile or a permanent intrinsic difficulty rating.

metrics.name: Item accuracy among attempted responses
metrics.inputs: the same item's full-correct and nonempty committed responses.
metrics.formula: C_q / A_q.
metrics.evidence: cohort N_q >= 100 and A_q >= 30.
metrics.action: distinguish low success from low willingness to attempt.
metrics.limitation: students select which questions to attempt, so this conditional rate is biased toward respondents and should always accompany the overall proportion.

metrics.name: Committed option-selection distribution
metrics.inputs: canonical options chosen in a single-choice item.
metrics.formula: count(option_j) / A_q for every option, with unanswered displayed separately.
metrics.evidence: N_q >= 100 and A_q >= 30; suppress option cells below 10 learners in shared views.
metrics.action: examine common distractors after solution release.
metrics.limitation: popularity alone cannot establish the underlying misconception, and shuffled option letters must be canonicalized.

metrics.name: Correct-response time percentile
metrics.inputs: the learner's visible time t and valid correct cohort times.
metrics.formula: 100 * count(cohort_time >= t) / N_correct; higher means faster-or-equal within correct responses.
metrics.evidence: cohort >= 100, N_correct >= 30 and valid personal time.
metrics.action: consider a shorter approved method.
metrics.limitation: correctness-conditioned selection and telemetry uncertainty prevent an ability-percentile interpretation.

metrics.name: Cohort median correct-response time
metrics.inputs: valid times from fully correct, first-exposure cohort responses.
metrics.formula: median(times), with the interquartile range.
metrics.evidence: cohort >= 100 and at least 30 usable correct times.
metrics.action: compare expected practice pacing with this specific question's observed distribution.
metrics.limitation: the median reflects this cohort and interface; it is not an official ideal time or universal time limit.

metrics.name: Personal-to-benchmark time ratio
metrics.inputs: valid personal time t and positive A37 median m.
metrics.formula: t / m.
metrics.evidence: A37 available and learner fully correct; otherwise provide personal time only.
metrics.action: inspect ratios substantially above a configurable threshold without chasing speed indiscriminately.
metrics.limitation: reading accommodations, language and solution style can affect timing; the ratio does not measure intelligence or concentration.

metrics.name: Item omission cohort rate
metrics.inputs: eligible delivered item attempts and final unanswered outcomes.
metrics.formula: U_q / N_q.
metrics.evidence: N_q >= 100; distinguish known unvisited from viewed omissions only with usable telemetry.
metrics.action: recognize questions the cohort often postpones.
metrics.limitation: omissions can reflect placement, section strategy or time pressure as well as difficulty; do not infer a single cause.

metrics.name: Item upper-minus-lower response difference
metrics.inputs: binary outcomes and rest-of-test net scores excluding this item.
metrics.formula: p_upper - p_lower for highest and lowest rest-score quartiles.
metrics.evidence: N >= 200, at least 50 per group and nonconstant rest scores; resolve boundary ties with documented fractional weights.
metrics.action: flag negative or unusual values for content review.
metrics.limitation: this descriptive discrimination signal is unstable under narrow score ranges and is not proof of a bad question.

metrics.name: Confidence calibration by bin
metrics.inputs: optional precommit probability ratings p and binary outcomes y.
metrics.formula: mean(p) and mean(y) within declared probability bins.
metrics.evidence: at least 20 rated items overall and 10 per displayed bin.
metrics.action: inspect confident errors and cautious successes.
metrics.limitation: self-reported probabilities are noisy; observed calibration does not establish a stable personal trait or justify universal guessing rules.

metrics.name: Binary Brier score
metrics.inputs: genuine precommit p in [0,1] and y equal to one for full correctness.
metrics.formula: mean((p - y)^2), with lower values indicating closer predictions.
metrics.evidence: at least 20 binary-rated distinct items; omit partial-credit items.
metrics.action: improve probability estimates using reviewed explanations.
metrics.limitation: item mix affects the score, and this is calibration evidence, not an intelligence or mastery score.

metrics.name: Low-confidence penalty exposure
metrics.inputs: precommit confidence, configurable threshold c and signed contributions.
metrics.formula: sum(max(-s_q,0) where p_q < c), plus the rated attempt count.
metrics.evidence: at least 10 genuinely rated attempts; default c = 0.20 is a product proposal.
metrics.action: review these choices against the marking policy.
metrics.limitation: low confidence does not prove blind guessing, and retrospective confidence is excluded.

metrics.name: Assumption-based expected marks
metrics.inputs: user-supplied correctness probability p, full reward a and wrong penalty magnitude b for a simple binary item.
metrics.formula: EV = p*a - (1-p)*b; break-even p = b/(a+b).
metrics.evidence: a+b > 0 and compatible marking rules.
metrics.action: explore practice decisions.
metrics.limitation: this is a hypothetical model; unknown p and time opportunity cost prevent guaranteed gains.

metrics.name: Confirmed error-cause distribution
metrics.inputs: learner-confirmed or teacher-reviewed causes for wrong items.
metrics.formula: count(cause) / number of labeled wrong items, with unknown and unlabeled counts separate.
metrics.evidence: at least five labeled errors before recommending a pattern.
metrics.action: select a targeted checking drill.
metrics.limitation: a chosen distractor does not prove a cause; preserve multiple possible causes and allow labels to be corrected.

metrics.name: Comparable first-attempt score change
metrics.inputs: latest score percentage and the preceding three comparable first-attempt score percentages.
metrics.formula: latest minus median(previous three).
metrics.evidence: four approved blueprint-matched tests with matching mode and scoring context.
metrics.action: inspect which topic outcomes accompany the change.
metrics.limitation: blueprint similarity does not guarantee equal difficulty; the difference is descriptive rather than a causal learning estimate.

metrics.name: Fresh concept accuracy change
metrics.inputs: distinct new concept-tagged items in two chronological windows.
metrics.formula: 100 * (C_recent/A_recent - C_prior/A_prior).
metrics.evidence: at least 20 items in each window, reviewed tags and no solution exposure.
metrics.action: verify whether the concept needs another drill.
metrics.limitation: changing difficulty and item selection can explain the gap; show counts and overlap checks.

metrics.name: Comparable score variability
metrics.inputs: score percentages from comparable first attempts.
metrics.formula: sample standard deviation sqrt(sum((x-mean)^2)/(n-1)).
metrics.evidence: at least five tests; display the individual observations.
metrics.action: review large swings and the associated exam conditions.
metrics.limitation: variability is not a personality, anxiety or attention diagnosis, and small test histories cannot establish a stable reliability profile.

metrics.name: Repeated-item score difference
metrics.inputs: first and later score for the same canonical item under the same effective key.
metrics.formula: mean(later_score - first_score) across paired items.
metrics.evidence: at least 10 pairs and known exposure state.
metrics.action: use improvement as feedback, then test a fresh related item.
metrics.limitation: remembered answers can drive the gain; do not mix repeated-item performance into first-exposure cohort percentiles.

metrics.name: Unresolved review backlog
metrics.inputs: wrong or omitted first-exposure items and explicit review-task states.
metrics.formula: count(open review tasks), with age since the attempt and topic breakdown.
metrics.evidence: at least one qualifying task; no mastery label.
metrics.action: schedule a manageable next review block.
metrics.limitation: closing a task records workflow completion, not concept mastery; automatic closure requires a clearly stated fresh-item check policy.

metrics.name: Recurring concept error count
metrics.inputs: distinct incorrect first-exposure items sharing a reviewed concept across sessions.
metrics.formula: count(distinct wrong canonical items), with attempted denominator.
metrics.evidence: at least five attempted concept items over three sessions before a recurring-pattern flag.
metrics.action: revisit the underlying method rather than memorizing individual answers.
metrics.limitation: related items and difficulty differences prevent treating the count as an independent diagnosis.

metrics.name: Fresh review-check success rate
metrics.inputs: new, approved counterpart items attempted after a documented review task.
metrics.formula: full-correct checks / attempted fresh checks.
metrics.evidence: at least 10 checks; exclude the original item and solution-exposed items.
metrics.action: decide whether to continue the drill or expand to harder examples.
metrics.limitation: selected checks can be easier than exams; success demonstrates these checks, not guaranteed transfer.

metrics.name: Delayed fresh-check accuracy
metrics.inputs: fresh counterpart items taken 14 days after review, allowing a declared plus/minus seven-day window.
metrics.formula: C_delayed/A_delayed.
metrics.evidence: at least 10 fresh checks with valid review and attempt dates.
metrics.action: schedule spaced review if errors recur.
metrics.limitation: this proposed schedule is configurable and later accuracy also reflects additional learning, item mix and missing follow-up participation.

metrics.name: Assigned prerequisite coverage
metrics.inputs: teacher-approved prerequisite tags and qualifying attempted practice.
metrics.formula: covered assigned tags / total assigned prerequisite tags; define covered as at least one valid attempt.
metrics.evidence: an explicit assignment and a positive tag count.
metrics.action: identify prerequisites not yet practiced.
metrics.limitation: coverage records exposure, not understanding; one attempt cannot certify readiness for a dependent concept.

metrics.name: Error-category marks-at-stake ceiling
metrics.inputs: confirmed error-category items, current score s_q and item maximum m_q.
metrics.formula: sum(m_q - s_q) for those wrong items.
metrics.evidence: reviewed cause labels and valid maxima; exact count always visible.
metrics.action: prioritize categories with several concrete examples.
metrics.limitation: this is a hindsight arithmetic ceiling, not predicted recoverable marks; fixing every error may require time and may not recur.

metrics.name: Released-solution consultation rate
metrics.inputs: eligible released review items and authorized solution-open events.
metrics.formula: distinct authorized opened solutions within the eligible review set / distinct released review items.
metrics.evidence: a positive released-item denominator and valid event access.
metrics.action: open relevant explanations for unreviewed errors.
metrics.limitation: opening a solution does not prove reading or understanding; no engagement event should be collected before the solution becomes accessible.

metrics.name: Observed solution review duration
metrics.inputs: visible solution-panel visits and capped heartbeat intervals.
metrics.formula: union of observed visible durations, with median duration per opened item.
metrics.evidence: at least five usable solution visits for a summary.
metrics.action: compare a review routine with its planned duration.
metrics.limitation: time on screen is not learning time, and copying a method is not demonstrated transfer.

metrics.name: Approved-key score revision impact
metrics.inputs: preserved historical report and newly approved grading revision.
metrics.formula: S_new - S_old, with every changed item contribution listed.
metrics.evidence: both reproducible ledgers and a published correction reason.
metrics.action: understand the corrected result and refreshed comparisons.
metrics.limitation: score changes from a key revision are not improvement or deterioration in the learner's ability.

metrics.name: Approved explanation availability
metrics.inputs: released delivered items and approved question-to-solution mappings.
metrics.formula: mapped approved explanations / released delivered items, with unavailable identifiers.
metrics.evidence: positive released-item denominator; count only approved mappings.
metrics.action: report missing explanations and revisit when corrected.
metrics.limitation: an available mapping does not guarantee explanatory quality, so preserve source review status and student feedback.

metrics.name: Usable timing evidence coverage
metrics.inputs: eligible items, reconciled visit events and timing quality flags.
metrics.formula: items with usable timing / eligible items; also show known timed duration / timer duration.
metrics.evidence: positive denominators and the declared quality policy.
metrics.action: understand why some speed suggestions are unavailable.
metrics.limitation: high coverage does not prove precise thinking time; missing events and visible-but-unfocused periods remain possible.
